DevOps.explanation: DevOps combines development and operations to deliver software faster and more reliably
points: Breaks down silos between dev, ops, QA, and security teams through shared responsibility
Emphasizes automation, continuous feedback, and small, frequent releases
Core practices: CI/CD, IaC, monitoring, blameless postmortems, and error budgets
DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR) measure performance
Foundation for modern cloud-native, microservices, and AI/ML delivery pipelines

CI/CD.explanation: Continuous Integration and Delivery automates building, testing, and deploying code changes
points: CI: every commit triggers automated build + unit/integration tests
CD: extends CI to produce production-ready artifacts (Continuous Delivery)
Continuous Deployment: automatically deploys every passing change to production
Reduces risk through small, frequent, reversible changes
Enables fast feedback loops critical for DevOps velocity

Docker.explanation: Docker packages apps and their dependencies into portable containers that run anywhere
points: Containerization standardizes runtime environment across dev, test, prod
Images are layered and immutable — enables caching and fast rebuilds
Docker Compose for local multi-container development
Docker Hub / private registries for distribution and versioning
Foundation layer for Kubernetes, serverless containers (Fargate, Cloud Run)

Kubernetes.explanation: Kubernetes orchestrates containers at scale handling deployment, scaling, and self-healing
points: De-facto standard for container orchestration since ~2017
Declarative model: describe desired state, control plane reconciles reality
Core objects: Pod, Deployment, Service, Ingress, ConfigMap, Secret
Horizontal Pod Autoscaling, Cluster Autoscaler, Vertical Pod Autoscaler
Extensible via CRDs, operators, Helm charts, and admission controllers

Infrastructure as Code.explanation: IaC manages servers and cloud resources using version-controlled code instead of manual steps
points: Enables reproducible, auditable, and peer-reviewed infrastructure
Treats infrastructure like application code — git commit, review, deploy
Tools: Terraform (multi-cloud), Pulumi (programming languages), AWS CDK, CloudFormation
Drift detection and reconciliation prevent configuration drift
Foundation for GitOps workflows and self-service platforms

Terraform.explanation: Terraform is the most popular IaC tool for provisioning cloud infrastructure declaratively
points: HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language) is domain-specific and readable
Provider ecosystem covers 1000+ services across clouds and SaaS
State file tracks real-world resources — stored remotely (S3 + DynamoDB lock)
Modules enable reusable, composable infrastructure patterns
Terraform Cloud / Enterprise adds collaboration, governance, and remote execution

Ansible.explanation: Ansible automates server configuration and application deployment using YAML playbooks
points: Agentless — uses SSH/WinRM, no software required on targets
Idempotent — safe to run repeatedly; only changes what needs changing
Roles and collections for reusable content
Excellent for configuration management, orchestration, and cloud provisioning
Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform adds enterprise features

GitHub Actions.explanation: GitHub Actions automates CI/CD workflows directly inside your GitHub repository
points: YAML workflows triggered by events (push, pull_request, schedule, workflow_dispatch)
Matrix strategy for parallel testing across versions/OS
Self-hosted runners for private infrastructure or special hardware
Integrated secrets, environments, and deployment protection rules

Jenkins.explanation: Jenkins is the most widely used open-source CI/CD automation server
points: Pipeline as code with Jenkinsfile (declarative or scripted)
Blue Ocean UI modernizes classic Jenkins experience
Still dominant in legacy enterprise environments

Monitoring.explanation: Monitoring tracks system health, performance metrics, and alerts when things go wrong
points: Four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation (Google SRE)
Alerting on symptoms (high error rate) vs causes
Essential for maintaining SLOs and quick MTTR

Observability.explanation: Observability uses logs, metrics, and traces to understand internal system behavior
points: Enables asking arbitrary questions about system state
High-cardinality data requires careful design (labels, sampling)
AI-powered anomaly detection and root-cause analysis emerging
Critical for microservices and distributed systems

Prometheus.explanation: Prometheus is an open-source metrics collection and alerting system for cloud-native apps
points: Federation and Thanos/Cortex for long-term storage and global view

Grafana.explanation: Grafana visualizes metrics and logs in beautiful dashboards for system monitoring
points: Supports Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch, InfluxDB, CloudWatch, and many more
Alerting engine with Slack, PagerDuty, email integrations
Grafana Cloud offers hosted version with free tier

ELK Stack.explanation: Elasticsearch, Logstash, and Kibana together collect, process, and visualize application logs
points: Logstash for complex parsing and enrichment
OpenSearch fork maintains open-source lineage after Elastic license change

Helm.explanation: Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes that simplifies deploying complex applications
points: Charts bundle Kubernetes manifests with templating
Artifact Hub central repository for charts
Essential for deploying databases, monitoring stacks, ingress controllers

Service Mesh.explanation: A service mesh handles inter-service communication, security, and observability transparently
points: Traffic shifting, retries, circuit breaking, timeouts
Observability: metrics, logs, traces without code changes
Istio, Linkerd, Consul most popular implementations

Istio.explanation: Istio is a popular open-source service mesh that adds traffic management and zero-trust security
points: Envoy proxy sidecar with rich feature set
VirtualService, DestinationRule, Gateway for traffic control
Mixer (legacy) → Telemetry v2 with direct Envoy metrics
Strong in enterprises with complex traffic requirements

GitOps.explanation: GitOps uses Git as the single source of truth for all infrastructure and deployment changes
points: Pull-based deployments — cluster pulls desired state

ArgoCD.explanation: ArgoCD continuously syncs Kubernetes clusters to match the desired state in Git
points: App of Apps pattern for multi-app deployments
Web UI and CLI for visibility and manual sync

Continuous Integration.explanation: CI automatically builds and tests code every time a developer pushes a change
points: Fast feedback loop on code quality

Continuous Delivery.explanation: CD automatically prepares code to be released to production after passing all tests

Continuous Deployment.explanation: Continuous deployment automatically pushes every passing change directly to production
points: No manual gates — highest automation level
Requires high confidence in automated tests
Used by high-performing teams (DORA elite performers)
Feature flags still used for controlled rollout

Container Registry.explanation: A container registry stores and distributes Docker images for deployment
points: Private registries: ECR, GCR, ACR, Harbor, Artifactory

Dockerfile.explanation: A Dockerfile is a script of instructions for building a Docker container image
points: FROM base image → RUN commands → COPY files → CMD/ENTRYPOINT
Multi-stage builds reduce final image size
BuildKit backend faster and more feature-rich

Pod.explanation: A Kubernetes Pod is the smallest deployable unit containing one or more containers
points: Containers in a pod share network namespace (localhost)
Ephemeral — pods are not rescheduled with same identity
Init containers run to completion before main containers
Sidecar pattern common for logging, proxy, monitoring

Deployment.explanation: A Kubernetes Deployment manages how many replicas of a Pod should run and updates them
points: Most common workload controller for stateless apps

Service.explanation: A Kubernetes Service provides a stable network address to route traffic to Pods
points: Headless service for direct pod access (StatefulSet)

Ingress.explanation: Kubernetes Ingress manages external HTTP traffic routing into cluster services
points: Ingress controller (NGINX, Traefik, ALB, Istio) required
Gateway API emerging as modern replacement

ConfigMap.explanation: ConfigMaps store non-secret configuration data that Kubernetes Pods can consume
points: As environment variables, command-line args, or files
Updates require pod restart unless mounted as volume

Secret.explanation: Kubernetes Secrets store sensitive data like passwords and API keys securely
points: Base64 encoded but not encrypted by default
Mounted as files or env vars
External secrets operators (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager)

Namespace.explanation: Kubernetes namespaces logically isolate resources within the same cluster
points: Resource quotas and limit ranges per namespace
RBAC can be namespace-scoped or cluster-wide

Rolling Update.explanation: Rolling updates gradually replace old Pod versions with new ones with zero downtime
points: Readiness probes prevent sending traffic to new pods too early
Revision history limit controls rollback depth

Horizontal Pod Autoscaling.explanation: HPA automatically scales Pod replicas up or down based on CPU or memory metrics
points: Uses metrics-server or custom metrics (Prometheus Adapter)
Multiple metrics and behavior tuning in newer versions
Requires readiness probes for safe scaling
Cluster Autoscaler complements for node scaling

Vertical Pod Autoscaling.explanation: VPA automatically adjusts CPU and memory requests for Pods based on actual usage
points: Can evict and recreate pods with new requests

Resource Limits.explanation: Resource limits cap how much CPU and memory a Kubernetes container can consume
points: Requests: guaranteed minimum, used for scheduling
Limits: hard cap — CPU throttled, memory OOMKilled
Best practice: set both requests and limits

Liveness Probe.explanation: Liveness probes detect and restart Pods that are stuck or deadlocked
points: Too aggressive can cause restart loops
Common pattern: health endpoint that checks dependencies

Readiness Probe.explanation: Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching Pods that are still starting up
points: Service only routes to ready pods
Initial delay important for slow-starting apps
Often same as liveness but with longer timeouts

Persistent Volume.explanation: Persistent Volumes give Kubernetes Pods durable storage that survives Pod restarts
points: StorageClass defines provisioner (EBS, EFS, GCS, etc.)
CSI drivers for modern storage integration

StatefulSet.explanation: StatefulSets manage Pods with stable identities and persistent storage for databases
points: Headless service for direct pod access

DaemonSet.explanation: DaemonSets ensure one Pod runs on every node for tasks like log collection or monitoring

CronJob.explanation: Kubernetes CronJobs run scheduled tasks on a cron schedule inside the cluster
points: Used for backups, report generation, cleanup
Job template defines the actual work

RBAC.explanation: Role-Based Access Control restricts what actions Kubernetes users and services can perform
points: Verbs: get, list, watch, create, update, patch, delete
Least privilege principle critical for security

Network Policy.explanation: Network policies control which Pods are allowed to communicate with each other
points: Default deny model — explicit allow rules
Requires CNI plugin support (Calico, Cilium, Weave)

Cert Manager.explanation: Cert-manager automates TLS certificate issuance and renewal inside Kubernetes
points: ACME support (Let's Encrypt) via HTTP-01 or DNS-01
Integrates with Ingress and Gateway API

Kustomize.explanation: Kustomize layers environment-specific Kubernetes config on top of base manifests without templating
points: No string substitution — preserves YAML structure
Preferred over Helm for simple customizations

CI Pipeline.explanation: A CI pipeline runs lint, test, build, and security checks on every code commit automatically
points: Stages: lint → unit test → integration test → build → scan
Failure blocks merge in protected branches

Artifact.explanation: A CI artifact is a build output like a Docker image or binary stored for deployment
points: Tagged with commit SHA, branch, version
Stored in registry (Docker) or artifact repository (JFrog, GitHub Packages)

Environment.explanation: Environments are isolated deployments like dev, staging, and production with separate configs
points: Promotes code through stages with increasing fidelity

Secrets Management.explanation: Secrets managers like Vault and AWS Secrets Manager store and rotate credentials securely

HashiCorp Vault.explanation: Vault centrally manages secrets, encrypts data, and issues short-lived credentials
points: Secrets engines: KV, database, PKI, AWS, GCP

Packer.explanation: Packer automates building identical machine images for multiple cloud platforms
points: Single source of truth for golden images
Builders: AWS AMI, Azure VHD, GCP image, Docker

Pulumi.explanation: Pulumi lets you write Infrastructure as Code using familiar programming languages
points: State stored in Pulumi Cloud or self-hosted
Strong for complex logic and abstraction

AWS CDK.explanation: AWS CDK defines cloud infrastructure using programming languages that compile to CloudFormation

CloudFormation.explanation: AWS CloudFormation provisions infrastructure declaratively through JSON or YAML templates
points: Stacks and stack sets for multi-account

Crossplane.explanation: Crossplane extends Kubernetes to provision and manage cloud resources from any provider
points: CRDs for cloud resources (RDS, S3, GCP buckets)

Blue-green Deployment.explanation: Blue-green spins up an identical environment and switches traffic over instantly
points: DNS or load balancer routing change
Ideal for stateful apps with careful data sync

Canary Deployment.explanation: Canary deployments send a small traffic percentage to new versions to test before full rollout

Feature Toggle.explanation: Feature toggles enable or disable features at runtime without new deployments
points: Technical debt if toggles not cleaned up

Observability Stack.explanation: An observability stack combines metrics, logs, and traces for full system visibility
points: Prometheus + Grafana + Loki + Tempo common open-source
Enables root cause analysis in distributed systems

OpenTelemetry.explanation: OpenTelemetry is the open standard for collecting traces, metrics, and logs from applications
points: Exporters to Jaeger, Zipkin, Prometheus, Loki

Jaeger.explanation: Jaeger is an open-source distributed tracing system for monitoring microservices

Zipkin.explanation: Zipkin is a distributed tracing system helping find where latency problems occur in services
points: Still widely used in Java ecosystems

Datadog.explanation: Datadog is a cloud monitoring platform combining metrics, logs, traces, and dashboards
points: Unified platform across infrastructure, APM, logs, security
Very popular in modern cloud-native companies

New Relic.explanation: New Relic provides full-stack observability and AI-powered alerts for engineering teams
points: One platform for APM, infrastructure, browser, mobile
Strong in enterprise and legacy environments

PagerDuty.explanation: PagerDuty routes alerts to on-call engineers and manages incident response workflows

Runbook.explanation: A runbook documents step-by-step procedures for handling specific operational incidents

Postmortem.explanation: A blameless postmortem analyzes what caused an incident to prevent it from happening again
points: Blameless culture — focus on systems not people
What happened → root cause → action items
Google SRE book and Etsy model influential

SRE.explanation: Site Reliability Engineering applies software engineering to operations and reliability problems
points: Error budgets balance reliability and velocity

Error Budget.explanation: An error budget defines how much downtime is acceptable before new releases are paused
points: SLO minus actual performance = error budget
Burn rate alerts when consuming too fast
Shared between SRE and product teams

SLO.explanation: Service Level Objectives define measurable reliability targets that teams commit to meeting
points: Expressed as percentage over time window (99.9% over 30 days)

SLI.explanation: Service Level Indicators are the specific metrics used to measure SLO performance
points: Good SLIs are measurable and user-facing
Four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation

On-call Rotation.explanation: On-call rotations share after-hours incident response duties across the engineering team

Incident Management.explanation: Incident management is the process of detecting, responding to, and resolving production issues
points: Incident commander, communications lead, ops lead roles
Major incident process with status updates

Mean Time to Recover.explanation: MTTR measures the average time from incident detection to full service restoration
points: Key DORA metric for elite performers
Target: hours → minutes for high performers

Mean Time Between Failures.explanation: MTBF measures the average time a system operates before experiencing a failure
points: Higher is better — indicates stable system
Harder to measure in distributed systems

Immutable Infrastructure.explanation: Immutable infrastructure replaces servers entirely instead of patching them in place

GitLab CI.explanation: GitLab CI is a built-in CI/CD system integrated directly into the GitLab platform

CircleCI.explanation: CircleCI is a cloud CI/CD platform known for fast builds and easy parallelism
points: Resource classes for different compute sizes

Buildkite.explanation: Buildkite runs CI pipelines on your own infrastructure with a cloud-based control plane
points: Hybrid model — agents on your infra

Tekton.explanation: Tekton is a Kubernetes-native CI/CD framework for building pipelines as custom resources
points: Used by Red Hat OpenShift Pipelines

Argo Workflows.explanation: Argo Workflows runs DAG and step-based pipelines as Kubernetes-native workflows
points: Used for ML workflows, data processing

Container Security.explanation: Container security scans images for vulnerabilities and enforces policies at runtime

Trivy.explanation: Trivy is an open-source vulnerability scanner for containers, file systems, and IaC configs
points: Misconfiguration detection for Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform

OPA.explanation: Open Policy Agent enforces security and compliance policies across cloud-native systems

Falco.explanation: Falco detects suspicious runtime behavior in Kubernetes containers in real time

Supply Chain Security.explanation: Supply chain security verifies the integrity of code and dependencies from source to production
points: Critical after SolarWinds and Log4j incidents

SBOM.explanation: A Software Bill of Materials lists every component and dependency in a software artifact
points: Becoming mandatory in supply chain security

Sigstore.explanation: Sigstore provides free tools to cryptographically sign and verify software artifacts
points: Adopted by Red Hat, Google, CNCF projects

Multi-cloud.explanation: Multi-cloud uses services from multiple cloud providers to avoid vendor lock-in
points: Different strengths: AWS breadth, GCP AI, Azure enterprise

Hybrid Cloud.explanation: Hybrid cloud combines on-premises infrastructure with public cloud services
points: Azure Arc, AWS Outposts, Google Anthos
Migration path from legacy data centers
Bursting to cloud for peak workloads

Cost Optimization.explanation: Cloud cost optimization right-sizes resources and eliminates waste to reduce infrastructure spend
points: Reserved capacity, spot instances, savings plans
Tools: AWS Cost Explorer, CloudHealth, nOps

Platform Engineering.explanation: Platform engineering builds internal developer platforms to improve team productivity and deployment speed

Internal Developer Platform.explanation: An IDP is a self-service layer that abstracts infrastructure complexity from application developers
points: Platform team owns IDP as product

Backstage.explanation: Backstage is Spotify's open-source developer portal for managing services and documentation

Dora Metrics.explanation: DORA metrics measure DevOps performance through deploy frequency, lead time, failure rate, and MTTR
points: Elite performers: multiple deploys/day, <1 hour lead time
Research-backed by Google Cloud DORA team

Shift Left Testing.explanation: Shift left testing moves quality checks earlier in the pipeline to catch bugs before deployment
points: Unit, integration, security, compliance in CI

Progressive Delivery.explanation: Progressive delivery releases features to increasing user percentages based on real-time health signals
points: Canary, blue-green, dark launch, A/B testing

Policy as Code.explanation: Policy as code enforces compliance and security rules automatically in CI/CD pipelines

Ephemeral Environments.explanation: Ephemeral environments spin up a full preview deployment per pull request and destroy it after merge
points: Tools: Gitpod, GitHub Codespaces, ArgoCD App of Apps

Dependency Scanning.explanation: Dependency scanning finds known vulnerabilities in third-party libraries automatically in CI
points: Integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps
Part of software supply chain security
